title: Interruptions that only people can make
subtitle: Echo sounded like a person to the detector; the rules were set so a person always wins the floor, the agent's own voice never does, the first word of an interruption is heard, and a false stop re-speaks instead of going quiet

stats.label: attack cases in an adversarial review before anyone heard the feature

of dead air after a false stop: the answer is spoken again

lede: A voice assistant that cannot be interrupted is a lecture. One that can be interrupted by its own echo is worse, because it stops mid-sentence for nobody. The voice engine runs full duplex, listening while it speaks, and the design problem is to make a person's interruption instant and everything else inert. While the agent is listening, it starts a turn the moment speech begins. While it is speaking, it is harder to stop: an interruption has to be sustained speech with a confidence the detector measures, because residual echo and room noise come back as brief, low-confidence bursts and a person does not.
quote: The agent's own voice can never take the floor from a person.
evidence: Barge-in and turn-taking for voice AI: a person can always take the floor, while the agent's own echo and other AI voices cannot.
Adversarial review of AI features: 18 attack cases reviewed before anyone heard the interruption feature.
Real-time audio cancellation: one confirmed interruption cancels reasoning, synthesis, the speaker queue and the Teams call together.
Recovery from false positives: a stop nobody made leaves 0 s of dead air, because the killed answer is spoken again word for word.
author: Corey James
